subject: technology
essential_question: Who is excluded by a design, and how do we find out before we ship it?
standards: Michigan Computer Science: Impacts of Computing
project_brief: Build a responsive, accessible multi-view interface with validated forms, then document an accessibility audit and a user-test revision log. This is the grade 9 culminating project for "Human-Centered and Accessible Interface Design" (ma-g9-technology-u05, unit 5), built around user research without private data, personas scenarios and requirements, semantic structure and responsive layout, forms validation and error handling without private data, and accessibility guidelines and assistive-technology testing. Build the interface or artifact described in this unit's project so that it stays usable with user research without private data, personas scenarios and requirements, semantic structure and responsive layout, and forms validation and error handling without private data, then run a short accessibility check against it and record one thing you changed as a result.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: user research without private data, personas scenarios and requirements, semantic structure and responsive layout, forms validation and error handling without private data, accessibility guidelines and assistive-technology testing, and usability testing consent and inclusive tradeoffs.
Meet the performance task as written: Build a responsive, accessible multi-view interface with validated forms, then document an accessibility audit and a user-test revision log.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Build the interface or artifact described in this unit's project so that it stays usable with user research without private data, personas scenarios and requirements, semantic structure and responsive layout, and forms validation and error handling without private data, then run a short accessibility check against it and record one thing you changed as a result.
test_or_check_criteria: Every claim or design choice in the submission can be traced to user research without private data or another named topic from this unit — nothing is left unexplained.
The submission runs, displays, or demonstrates correctly on at least two different sample inputs or scenarios the student chooses.
No real password, API key, account credential, precise location, or other real personal/system data appears anywhere in the submission — fictional or sandbox examples only.
The student can explain, in their own words, why each step or decision was made, not just that it works.
Every interactive element is reachable and usable without a mouse, and every image or icon has a text alternative.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: This project never touches a real account, a real password or API key, a live production system, or another person's real data. Use fictional names, sandbox environments, local files, or already-approved sample data throughout. Submit code, screenshots of your own sandbox, diagrams, or a written walkthrough — a live public deployment is never required.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Never request, store, or submit a real password, API key, access token, or other real credential; use only fictional accounts and sandboxed or offline systems.
remediation: If the project stalls, step back to the smallest version of the task: rebuild just the part covering user research without private data in isolation, using a worked example from this unit as a model, then re-attach it to the full project once that smaller piece works and you can explain why.
extension: Once the core project is working, extend it to handle a new constraint or edge case related to personas scenarios and requirements, or compare two different approaches to the same problem and explain the real tradeoff between them in your own words.
